svg.title: Two DAGs around one motion planner
svg.desc: The textbook pipeline (task assignment, MAPF, ADG, executor) above the scheduler's: the event DAG is a task graph built before any timing, CHUGG plans timed motions from it, and only then is the action DAG (the ADG) built from CHUGG's trajectories.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The event DAG is not an ADG. It is also a DAG of discrete changes with "must happen before" edges, and a few of its edges are spatial (AddNodeArrivalDeps, path repair), but it is a task-level precedence graph made before any timing. The ADG in the

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: standard sense is step 3, built from CHUGG's output, and it inherits the event edges.

g.text: Stages 1 and 3 are in scheduler.cpp (Plan, ResponseFromTrajectories); stage 2 is motion_planner (chugg_common.cpp, chugg_sequential.cpp), called from PlanMotions. Dispatch is not in the snapshots.

g.text: Two DAGs around one motion planner

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Order of the pipeline is MAPF -> ADG -> executor, as in the literature. What is different is step 1: CHUGG's input is a precedence graph between events of many entities, not one goal per robot.
